plan.contextChunk: This figure sets three side-by-side panels, (a), (b), and (c), showing one small undirected graph and two ways of storing it. Panel (a) draws the graph as five gray circles numbered 1 through 5, with 1 at the upper left, 2 at the upper right, 3 at the far right, 4 at the lower middle, and 5 at the lower left, joined by seven straight edges: 1-2, 1-5, 2-5, 2-3, 2-4, 3-4, and 4-5. Panel (b) gives the adjacency-list form as a vertical array of five gray cells indexed 1 to 5, each holding a pointer arrow into a horizontal chain of two-field records whose right field is either an arrow onward or a diagonal slash marking the end. Row 1 chains 2 then 5; row 2 chains 1, 5, 3, 4; row 3 chains 2 then 4; row 4 chains 2, 5, 3; row 5 chains 4, 1, 2. Panel (c) gives the adjacency matrix as a bordered five-by-five grid of zeros and ones with rows and columns both headed 1 through 5, zeros along the diagonal and entries symmetric across it. Laying the picture beside the two tables lets a single edge be found three ways, and it makes plain that each undirected edge is stored twice.

demo_steps.title: Same graph, three encodings
demo_steps.narration: The left panel is the graph itself, the middle panel stores each vertex's neighbors in a linked list, and the right panel stores the same information as a 5-by-5 matrix. Focus on any representation to see that the neighbor relationships match across all three.

demo_steps.title: Trace one edge
demo_steps.narration: Click an edge such as 2-4 in the graph, or click either of its matrix 1s. The demo highlights edge 2-4, the list record 4 in vertex 2's list, the list record 2 in vertex 4's list, and the symmetric matrix cells (2,4) and (4,2).

demo_steps.title: Focus on one vertex's neighborhood
demo_steps.narration: Switch focus to the adjacency list and select vertex 2. Its neighbors 1, 3, 4, and 5 appear as list records, as graph edges incident on vertex 2, and as 1s across row and column 2 of the matrix.

demo_steps.title: Edit an undirected edge
demo_steps.narration: Select two vertices and press add/remove. The graph line appears or disappears, and the storage updates in pairs: one record in each affected adjacency list and two symmetric matrix entries.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: In an undirected graph, each edge {u,v} is a single relationship but is stored twice: v appears in u's adjacency list, u appears in v's adjacency list, and the matrix has matching 1s at (u,v) and (v,u).
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Create three horizontally aligned panels matching the textbook layout. Use light gray filled circles and cells with black outlines, black graph edges, black arrows in the linked-list panel, and a simple black-bordered matrix. Keep the graph geometry recognizable: 1 upper left, 2 upper center-right, 3 far right, 4 lower center-right, 5 lower left, with the seven listed edges. In the adjacency-list panel, show each linked record as a two-field box: the left field contains the neighbor number and the right field contains either a pointer arrow to the next record or a diagonal slash for null. In the matrix panel, place row and column labels 1 through 5 outside the grid and show symmetric 1s for all graph edges with zeros on the diagonal. Use strong but readable highlights: selected vertices in blue, selected edge in orange, corresponding adjacency-list records in yellow, and symmetric matrix cells outlined or filled lightly in the same edge color.

authoredContext: The adjacency-list representation of a graph G D .V; E/ consists of an array Adj of jV j lists, one for each vertex in V . For each u 2 V , the adjacency list AdjŒu contains all the vertices _x0017_ such that there is an edge .u; _x0017_/ 2 E. That is, AdjŒu consists of all the vertices adjacent to u in G. (Alternatively, it may contain pointers to these vertices.) Since the adjacency lists represent the edges of a graph, in pseudocode we treat the array Adj as an attribute of the graph, just as we treat the edge set E. In pseudocode, therefore, we will see notation such as G:AdjŒu. Figure 22.1(b) is an adjacency-list representation of the undirected graph in Figure 22.1(a).

discrepancies: The underlying graph, adjacency-list records, and adjacency-matrix values are mostly correct, but the rendered default figure is compressed into the left portion of the page because a large control panel occupies the right side; the source is a full-width static triptych.
Text and numeric labels are noticeably smaller at the rendered inline size than in the source, especially the matrix entries, adjacency-list values, and panel labels.
The visible guided-demo UI, narration, dropdown, and edge-edit button are not part of the source figure and change the overall composition of the default view.

The focus-representation control does not visibly emphasize an entire representation in a source-like way; it mostly selects/highlights vertices or edges, which is pedagogically useful but not a faithful static replacement.
evaluation.notes: The three graph encodings are structurally accurate and conceptually correct, but the default view is visually shrunken by UI chrome and the labels are less legible than the source.
action_items: Dock the UI below the figure or make it collapsible so the default visual triptych can occupy the full available width like the source image.
Increase effective figure scale or font sizes so node numbers, list entries, matrix entries, and panel labels remain comfortably readable at inline size.
Add a reset-to-original button after edge edits so users can easily return to the exact textbook graph, list, and matrix.
Make the representation-focus dropdown produce a clear visual emphasis on the selected panel, or remove it from the default if the goal is a static drop-in replacement.
